Ongoing studies of reproductive and nursery success in lower Howard Creek are presently being performed by South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources. Sufficient time has not exapsed since last winter's spawning for the results to be conclusive. Since there is a reproductive rainbow trout fishery in Howard Creek, it can be safely assumed that spawning will be successful. The biological productivity of lower Howard is presently reduced due to sedimentation. Therefore, the nursery success this summer will be reduced proportionately. The increasing value and popularity of this new and unique resource makes it imperative that sufficient time for studies be allowed prior to a decision on licensing. In no other way can the values involved be realistically assessed.
An analysis of the Applicant's proposal to augment the flow of Howard Creek has been performed. The intent is to use water from Bad Creek Reservoir by means of a conduit-control valve system. Water of the same temperature as the stream will not be available in the Bad Creek Reservoir due to pumping back of Jocassee waters, and the temperature increasing factors discussed previously.
